name: Iddo
overview: The name Iddo appears in Scripture as a multifaceted figure connected to the restoration of Israel, serving as a prophet, priest, and leader among the Jews. He is notably identified as the father of Zechariah the prophet, who, along with Haggai, encouraged the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem under Persian decree (Ezra 5:1, 6:14; Zechariah 1:1). Additionally, Iddo is recognized as the chief of the Jews at Casiphia, entrusted with organizing ministers for the house of God (Ezra 8:17). His lineage and roles emphasize God's providential hand in preserving faithful leadership during the return from exile (Nehemiah 12:4, 12:16).
